newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha edges up but demand for N+A falls down.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha edges up but demand for N+A falls down.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices edged slightly higher on Wednesday after a bounce in crude oil but traders said demand for heavier material was drying up after weakness in the gasoline market.

Traders also cited rumours that material may be sent from Central and South America, namely Venezuela and Mexico, to Northwest Europe due to favourable arbitrage opportunities. This could not be confirmed.

June swaps rose $1 to $179.50/$180.50 a tonne, tracking a bounce in Brent crude futures from the 12-month lows registered on Tuesday. July swaps held a 50-cent backwardation at $179/$180. Traders noted continued resilience in the naphtha to crude crack spread.

Cargoes were notionally valued at $183/$185 cif after a 10-15,000 tonne cargo of light virgin naphtha traded late Tuesday at $184, traders said. Demand for pipeline spec material was also seen in the market for the second straight day.
"The N+A (naphthenic and aromatic) market is not there," a broker said. "End-users are not aggressively in the market and are fairly well covered for June."

With a drop of more than 2.5 cents a gallon in NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures on Tuesday and bearish sentiment in the NWE gasoline barge market, traders said it was becoming uneconomical to buy N+A naphtha material for reformers. The heavier material is a feedstock for making gasoline.
"We are quite relaxed and sitting back to see what happens," said one end-user. "I also expect some naphtha in Europe with the U.S. (prices) falling rapidly."
The NWE market was also well supplied with two cargoes from Riga, one from Ventspils and two from Tallinn on offer, he said. Each cargo was 5-10,000 tonnes.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4095 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
